title: Release audit: README.md still documents `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` for the install command and fo
summary: Update both documented commands to the current release installer (v0.1.1 or a versionless latest URL) and add a README guard test that asserts the install and uninstall commands use the release installer.
requirements: R1: README.md contains no reference to the `v0.1.0` install script URL (`.../v0.1.0/install.sh`), in the install command or anywhere else.
R2: The README install command and the README uninstall command reference exactly the same install-script URL, and that URL is the only install-script URL in README.md.

R3: The install-script URL in README.md points at the release whose behavior the documentation describes (the current release, i.e. the v0.1.1 release referenced by the audit finding), not at an earlier tag. The version selector appears exactly once in the URL and both commands inherit it.
R4: No other README content changes: the surrounding prose, command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | bash`), options and section structure stay as they are, except for the URL itself.

R5: If the chosen URL names a release tag that is not yet published at commit time, the README names the newest published tag instead and the discrepancy is recorded in the task report; README must never advertise a tag that does not resolve.

R6: The existing test suite passes, and tests/test_readme_install.py either already fails on the stale URL (and therefore now passes) or is extended to assert R1 and R2 without weakening any existing assertion.
R7: No change to install.sh, forge_code/*, pyproject.toml or the release directories is introduced by this task.
acceptance: A1: A grep for `v0.1.0/install.sh` in README.md returns nothing.
A2: All install-script URLs found in README.md are identical, and there are at least two of them (one in the install command, one in the uninstall command).
A3: The version selector in the README install-script URL equals the version documented as the current release, and the URL is fetchable (HTTP 200) from the public repository.
A4: The README diff contains only URL changes, reviewable as a small, self-contained change.
A5: `python -m pytest` passes for the whole repository, including tests/test_readme_install.py.
A6: `git diff --name-only` lists only README.md and, optionally, tests/test_readme_install.py.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

result.summary:
Rewrote the README install documentation onto the single versionless canonical install-script URL `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh` and replaced the tag-pinned guard with a text-only canonical-URL guard.

Changes:
- README.md: the `## Install`, `### Update` and `### Uninstall` commands now all use the same versionless default-branch URL; the command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | sh`, `| sh -s -- --uninstall`) and every other line are unchanged. The diff is exactly three URL substitutions, no tag-pinned install-script path remains, and no release version is named next to the commands.
- tests/test_readme_install.py: the guard is now built on `INSTALL_URL` (versionless) instead of `INSTALL_TAG = "v0.1.1"`. `assert_single_install_script_url` rejects a stale tag path (`/v0.1.0/install.sh`), any tag-pinned install-script path (`/v<tag>/install.sh`), a missing URL (fewer than two), and any URL other than the one canonical string. Added `test_no_tag_pinned_install_script_url`, `test_another_branch_install_script_url_is_rejected`, `test_a_missing_install_script_url_is_rejected`, and kept `test_stale_install_script_url_is_rejected` / `test_divergent_install_script_url_is_rejected`, both proving rejection by `assertRaises(AssertionError)` on the guard itself, not by message wording. The module imports only `re`, `unittest` and `pathlib`: no network, `urllib`, `http.client`, `requests`, `socket` or `subprocess`.
- tests/test_cli.py: `ReadmeTest::test_readme_has_a_pinned_install_command` now expects `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh | sh` and additionally asserts no tag-pinned path; the former `test_readme_has_no_default_branch_install` (which forced the tag pin) was replaced by `test_readme_has_no_tag_pinned_install`, which asserts every raw.githubusercontent.com line is the canonical URL and none is tag-pinned. No other assertion was weakened.
- CHANGELOG.md: the single existing `## [Unreleased]` → `### Fixed` bullet now describes the delivered change (versionless current installer for install/update/uninstall, no stale tag path, guard on reintroduction); wording no longer names v0.1.1.

Verification:
- `python -m pytest -q` → 214 passed, 137 subtests passed in 140.84s.
- No `v0.1.0/install.sh` or `v0.1.1/install.sh` string in README.md; both commands share one URL.
- Live fetch of the canonical URL: HTTP 200, 29597 bytes, from `raw.githubusercontent.com` resolved against the `main` branch (the repository branch is `main`; `git tag --list` shows no published v0.1.1 tag, so a tag-pinned URL would 404 — verified v0.1.1/install.sh returns 404).
- Uninstall invocation confirmed against `install.sh`: the `main()` case `--uninstall)` dispatching to `uninstall()` (install.sh lines 962-963), documented in `usage()` at line 0115 and 0123.
- `git diff --name-only` shows the four task files plus the pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes in `install.sh` and `tests/test_install.py`, which this task did not touch and did not commit.; the completion step could not decide which uncommitted files belong to the task
assumptions: Kept the single `## [Unreleased]` bullet in CHANGELOG.md and only corrected its wording, as the specification requires one bullet rather than a second entry.

Replaced `ReadmeTest::test_readme_has_no_default_branch_install` because its premise (raw.githubusercontent URLs must contain `/v`) is exactly the stale-tag policy the new specification forbids; the replacement `test_readme_has_no_tag_pinned_install` asserts the stronger canonical-URL contract instead.
The `## Tests` section's `v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]` link was left untouched: it is a release tarball, not an install-script URL, and R4 forbids other README changes.
The canonical URL tracks the `main` branch tip rather than a release tag; this is the trade-off the specification accepts to avoid advertising an unpublished tag.
spec_feedback: the planner accepted the specification issue and rewrote the specification; implement the new version
feedback: Implement the rewritten specification (v2) as written; do not preserve the v0.1.1 pin that only satisfied the previous version.

README.md: replace every install-script URL, in the `## Install` command, the `### Update` command and the `### Uninstall` command, with the single canonical versionless URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh, keeping the command shape unchanged.
README.md: leave no tag-pinned install-script path anywhere (no `v0.1.0/install.sh`, no `v0.1.1/install.sh`) and confirm no release version is named in prose next to the commands.

tests/test_readme_install.py: guard README.md as text against the canonical versionless URL — reject a stale tag-pinned path, a divergent URL, and a missing URL — without any network access, `urllib`, `http.client`, `requests`, `socket` or `subprocess` use; keep `test_stale_install_script_url_is_rejected` and `test_divergent_install_script_url_is_rejected` proving the rejection by the guard raising, not by message wording.
tests/test_cli.py: update `ReadmeTest::test_readme_has_a_pinned_install_command` to expect the versionless canonical command and to fail on any tag-pinned path; weaken no other assertion.

CHANGELOG.md: the existing `## [Unreleased]` bullet must describe the delivered change (versionless current installer, no stale tag path); do not add a second bullet, and correct its wording if it still names v0.1.1.

Before finishing, verify install.sh actually supports the documented uninstall invocation, record the supporting line of install.sh in the report, run the repository test suite, and confirm `git diff --name-only` lists only README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py, tests/test_cli.py and CHANGELOG.md; leave unrelated working-tree files (install.sh, tests/test_check_cleanup.py, tests/test_install.py) uncommitted.

result.last_summary: README.md now documents one install-script URL, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh, in the `## Install` command, the `### Update` command and the `### Uninstall` command (`| sh -s -- --uninstall`); the only README change is the URL in those lines, so no `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` reference remains. tests/test_cli.py's `ReadmeTest::test_readme_has_a_pinned_install_command` now pins the full v0.1.1 command instead of the v0.1.0 URL. CHANGELOG.md keeps exactly one English `## [Unreleased]` bullet recording the fix. tests/test_readme_install.py keeps the text-only guard built from the single `INSTALL_TAG = "v0.1.1"` constant and gains the two named rejection tests required by the spec: `test_stale_install_script_url_is_rejected` feeds the guard's own `assert_single_install_script_url` a document carrying `/v0.1.0/install.sh`, and `test_divergent_install_script_url_is_rejected` feeds it a document whose second install-script URL names another tag; both require the same assertion the positive path uses to raise, so the guard is proven by behaviour rather than message wording. The module imports only `re`, `unittest` and `pathlib` and fetches nothing. Verified with `python -m unittest -v tests.test_readme_install tests.test_cli.ReadmeTest` (37 tests OK) and the full `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (211 tests OK, ~141 s). Note: the documented installer URL currently answers HTTP 404 because the v0.1.1 tag is not published yet; that is recorded under spec_issues.; uncommitted files outside the contract: install.sh, tests/test_check_cleanup.py, tests/test_install.py
